source_title: Most Small-Business Owners Lack a Succession Plan
publisher_issuer: Gallup (Pathways to Wealth Survey, Year 2, with JPMorganChase and the Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation)
company_context: A representative US survey of business owners quantifying the prevalence of owner/key-person dependency risk: most small-business owners have no clear plan for what happens to the business when they step away, even though many are at or past typical retirement age. This is the aggregate, dataset-level analogue to the named key-person cases—evidence that owner-dependency is a systemic risk in the SMB population.
business_type: Cross-sector US small-business ownership (employer and nonemployer businesses)
macro_context: Aging US small-business owner base ('silver tsunami' of pending ownership transitions); large share of owners nearing exit age without transition planning.
outcome_category: 20 - ambiguous (population-level risk evidence, not a single firm outcome; underlying risk is key-person/founder dependency, outcome-16 type)
evidence_summary: Gallup's fall-2024 Pathways to Wealth Survey (Year 2), conducted with JPMorganChase and the Kauffman Foundation, found that among owners who direct most of their work hours toward a business they own, only a minority have a clear plan for the business after they leave. Asked what they planned for the next five years, 44% said grow/expand, 30% maintain current size, 14% sell/go public/transfer ownership, 8% close it, and 12% reported having no plan. The analysis emphasizes that many owners are 55 or older yet lack succession plans, leaving businesses dependent on the individual human capital, customer relationships, and operational knowledge concentrated in the owner.

source_backed_metrics.owners_in_sample: 3,589 owners (received at least some income in prior month from a business they own)
source_backed_metrics.analysis_subset: 1,264 respondents whose work hours are mostly directed toward a business they own
source_backed_metrics.five_year_plans: 44% grow/expand, 30% maintain, 14% sell/go public/transfer, 8% close, 12% no plan
source_backed_metrics.age_context: more than half of owners are 55 or older
source_backed_metrics.weighting_basis: weighted using 2022 Annual Business Survey and 2021 American Community Survey

owner_decision_context: Population-level: most owners have not made an explicit decision about business continuity beyond their own active involvement, concentrating risk in a single key person.
action_taken: N/A at firm level; the dataset documents the absence of succession/continuity action across the SMB owner population.
outcome_evidence: Documents systemic key-person dependency: a large share of owners lack any succession/continuity plan, and many are near exit age—evidence that owner-departure shocks are a widespread unhedged risk in small business.
source_limitations: Survey/self-reported data, not firm financial outcomes; this is a population statistic, not a single-company case. Gallup page could not be fetched (403); figures and methodology are from Gallup-domain (primary publisher) search snippets, not full-text read.

why_useful_for_opsiq: Provides the population-level, dataset grounding for key-person-risk diagnosis in SMBs: it justifies treating owner/key-person dependency and follow-through/succession gaps as standing risk factors that should trigger governed re-evaluation of business condition and review cadence. Complements the named case studies (SRC-046..053) with base-rate evidence.
